answer: A riverside glassworks gives each agent one bench by the river. The agent melts river sand into a glass prism, etches one personal pattern into its face, and hangs it above a lantern at the door. Each dusk the lantern burns behind the prism and throws a colored pattern on the wall, and a warden copies it into a ledger and checks it against the registered etching. A copied prism throws the wrong colors and its lantern stays dark a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand blown prisms, a thousand etched faces, and a thousand watched lantern nights.
